title: Preamble
notes_md:
# Preamble

The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution, based on the **Objectives Resolution** moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.

## Text and keywords

It declares India a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic** and secures to all citizens **Justice** (social, economic, political), **Liberty** (of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship), **Equality** (of status and opportunity) and **Fraternity** (assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation).

The words **socialist**, **secular** and **integrity** were added by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976** — the only amendment to the Preamble so far.

The date in the Preamble — **26 November 1949** — is the date of adoption; the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950.

## Is the Preamble part of the Constitution?

- **Berubari Union case (1960):** the Supreme Court held the Preamble is *not* a part of the Constitution.
- **Kesavananda Bharati case (1973):** overruled Berubari — the Preamble *is* a part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368, subject to the **basic structure** doctrine.
- **LIC of India case (1995):** reaffirmed that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.

The Preamble is **non-justiciable**: its provisions are not enforceable in courts, and it is neither a source of power nor a limitation on it — but it aids interpretation of ambiguous constitutional provisions.

## Sources of its ideals

- Liberty, equality, fraternity — **French Revolution**
- Republic — France
- Justice (social, economic, political) — Russian Revolution ideals

title: Fundamental Duties
notes_md:
# Fundamental Duties

Fundamental Duties are contained in **Part IVA**, which consists of a single article — **Article 51A**. They were added by the **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976** on the recommendation of the **Swaran Singh Committee**, and are inspired by the Constitution of the **erstwhile USSR**.

## Count and evolution

- The Swaran Singh Committee recommended **8** duties; the 42nd Amendment enacted **10**.
- The **86th Amendment Act, 2002** added the **11th duty** — Article 51A(k): a parent or guardian shall provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the ages of **6 and 14 years**.

## Key features

- Apply **only to citizens**, not to foreigners (unlike some Fundamental Rights that extend to all persons).
- **Non-justiciable**: not enforceable by courts; no penalty is prescribed by Article 51A itself. Parliament may enforce specific duties through ordinary law (e.g., Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971).
- They serve as an interpretive aid — courts may use them to test the reasonableness of laws.

## Notable duties (Article 51A)

- (a) abide by the Constitution, respect the National Flag and National Anthem
- (g) protect and improve the **natural environment** including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and have compassion for living creatures
- (h) develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
- (j) strive towards excellence in all spheres
- (k) provide education opportunities to children aged 6-14 (added 2002)

title: Vice-President
notes_md:
# Vice-President

**Article 63** provides for a Vice-President of India — the second highest constitutional office, modelled on the American Vice-President.

## Functions

- **Ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (Article 64); presides over its sittings but votes only to resolve a tie.
- **Acts as President** (Article 65) when a vacancy occurs (death, resignation, removal) — for a maximum of **six months**, within which a new President must be elected. Also discharges the President's functions during temporary absence or illness.
- While acting as President, he does not preside over the Rajya Sabha; the Deputy Chairman does.

## Election (Article 66)

- Electoral college: **elected AND nominated members of BOTH Houses of Parliament**. State legislatures play **no part** — the key contrast with the President's election (which includes elected MLAs and excludes nominated members).
- System: **proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote**, voting by **secret ballot**.
- Election disputes go to the **Supreme Court**, whose decision is final.

## Qualifications, term, removal

- Citizen of India, at least **35 years** of age, qualified for election as a member of the **Rajya Sabha** (contrast: President — Lok Sabha).
- Term: **5 years**; eligible for re-election; resignation addressed to the **President**.
- Removal: resolution of the **Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority, agreed to by the Lok Sabha** with 14 days' prior notice. The Constitution specifies **no grounds** for removal — and no formal impeachment.
- Oath administered by the **President** or a person appointed by him.

**First Vice-President:** Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1952-62).
